record_body:
ACCOUNT SUMMARY
- Existing Redwood customer (direct contract today) exploring moving spend to AWS Marketplace to consolidate cloud spend + use AWS committed spend/credits.
- Current usage: Hosted API (chat + embeddings) powering in-product “case summary” and internal support tooling.
- Expansion motion: potentially add Dedicated capacity for peak weekday traffic + improved data isolation; keep Hosted for dev/test.

FIRMOGRAPHICS / ENV
- HQ: US (multi-region users; strong preference for us-east-1 first, with roadmap to eu-west-1).
- Cloud posture: AWS-first. They have a strict payer-account policy; procurement wants all software spend through 1 payer.
- Data: Mix of customer support tickets + internal runbooks. No regulated data stated, but they treat support artifacts as “sensitive” and require auditability.

CURRENT FOOTPRINT (AS-IS)
- Contract: direct (Net 30). Annual commit with overage.
- Workloads:
  - Chat: agent-assist + summarization (streaming responses required)
  - Embeddings: doc-search / semantic retrieval (batch jobs nightly + on-demand)
- Requirements noted on last QBR:
  - Latency: p95 < 1.5s for typical chat turns (non-longform)
  - Reliability: “can’t break agent workflow” during incidents; want clear fallback guidance
  - Governance: SSO/SAML, audit logs, and retention controls (esp. for logs)

WHY MARKETPLACE (THEIR WORDS)
- “We’re trying to put all vendors through AWS Marketplace so procurement stops blocking renewals.”
- Wants AWS Marketplace invoices for internal chargeback.
- They believe they can apply AWS credits/EDP commitments to the spend.

PROCUREMENT / BILLING CONSTRAINTS (NOTES)
- Co-term / renewal alignment: They do NOT want overlapping payments (direct renewal is early Q2). Prefer marketplace start aligned to renewal, or a clean amendment/true-up plan.
- Discounting: They asked if current discounted rate can be reflected in Marketplace. Flagged that Marketplace has constraints; need Finance-approved guidance on allowable pricing floors and whether we can use private offers.
- Invoice descriptions: Their finance team needs consistent SKU naming (Hosted vs Dedicated; add-ons separate). “The line items have to match what we book to cost centers.”
- Multiple AWS accounts: They have more than one AWS payer due to acquisitions; need to confirm which payer will purchase and ensure entitlement maps to the correct Redwood org. Risk of linking to the wrong org mentioned (ref: prior industry issues).
- Credits: They asked about pre-paid credits and whether marketplace purchase can fund multiple Redwood orgs (answer: likely no; need to keep 1:1 mapping per org / payer to reduce support risk).

SECURITY / COMPLIANCE QUESTIONS (OPEN)
- Asked for: SOC 2 handling, KMS language, audit log coverage, and data retention defaults.
- They specifically asked whether audit logs include “admin actions + provisioning events” (we pointed them to updated Marketplace Security FAQ and clarified shared responsibility).

RECENT ACTIVITY TIMELINE
- 2025-11-12: CSM QBR (Jasmine Liu) — early signal they will push procurement to Marketplace in next renewal cycle.
- 2025-12-03: SE call (Markus Klein) — Dedicated capacity discussion; asked whether Dedicated can be purchased via AWS Marketplace and how capacity commitments work.
- 2026-01-09: Finance escalation: invoice confusion on marketplace vs direct contract terminology (linked support ticket SUP-18447).
- 2026-01-22: Internal Redwood sync (Jordan Blake + Laura Bennett + Cole Summers) — discussed private offer approach and co-term mechanics; action to confirm SKU mapping for Hosted commit + any add-ons.
- 2026-02-04: Shared customer-facing draft FAQ + “buy via marketplace” overview sent; customer requested a single page they can forward to Procurement.
- 2026-02-18: Customer email: wants to start AWS Marketplace process in March if we can guarantee clean activation + correct org mapping on day 1.

RISKS / WATCHOUTS
- Entitlement mapping: If they purchase under the wrong payer, risk of mis-linked entitlement and delayed activation (high escalation likelihood).
- Region: They are us-east-1 first; need to ensure the marketplace listing copy and onboarding flow are explicit about region availability and how to request additional regions.
- Add-ons: They asked if retention/longer observability retention can be added later via Marketplace (needs clarity on upgrade/downgrade policy).

NEXT STEPS (TACTICAL)
- Confirm which AWS payer account will purchase; collect AWS Account ID + payer details.
- Propose option A: marketplace start at renewal; option B: short bridge term + marketplace start date (Finance + Legal to bless).
- Send final SKU table (Hosted API commit + any compliance/retention add-on) + expected invoice descriptors.
- Schedule procurement call with their Finance/Procurement + their AWS rep if needed; align on private offer timeline.
